issue: No heating since last night — occupant is 82 and uses oxygen (3 Church Street)

body:
From: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@example.com>
To: maintenance@riverbank-lettings.example.com
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 07:48:12 +0100
Subject: 3 Church Street — no heating or hot water since last night, mum is 82

Hello,

I'm writing on behalf of my mother, Margaret Hughes, who is your tenant at
3 Church Street, Twickenham (ground floor flat). The boiler cut out
yesterday evening around 7pm and hasn't come back on. There's no heating
and no hot water. The display shows a flashing "E133" and the pressure
gauge is sitting at about 0.5. I've tried the reset button twice as the
manual says and it fires up for a few seconds and then cuts out again.

I need to stress that my mum is 82, she has COPD and uses an oxygen
concentrator overnight, and she really cannot be in a cold flat. It was
about 14 degrees in there this morning. I've brought over a couple of
blankets and she's sitting in her coat, but I can't stay with her all day
as I have to be at work by 10.

Please could someone come out today. She's at home all day and I can be
reached on 07700 900505; my mum doesn't always hear the phone. The front
door has a keysafe but I'd rather someone phoned first so she isn't
startled.

I know Dr Osei likes to be told about things, so please do let her know,
but honestly we just need an engineer as soon as possible.

Thank you,
Claire Hughes

summary: Riverbank Lettings — URGENT, 3 Church Street. Thank you for reporting the boiler fault this morning. We are treating this as an emergency and are arranging a Gas Safe heating engineer to attend today. In the meantime, please: (1) stop pressing the boiler reset button — repeated resets on a locked-out boiler can make things worse; leave the boiler switched off at its control; (2) do not attempt to repressurise or open up the boiler yourselves; (3) keep Mrs Hughes in one room with the door closed, warmly dressed and with warm (non-alcoholic) drinks; (4) if you smell gas at any time, do not touch electrical switches, open the windows, leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999. We have your note that there is a keysafe but that the engineer should telephone 07700 900505 first — we will pass that on. We will confirm the engineer's attendance window as soon as the contractor comes back to us, and a manager will call to check on Mrs Hughes today.

summary: Dr Osei — emergency at 3 Church Street, Twickenham, reported 08/10/2026 07:48. Total loss of heating and hot water since ~19:00 yesterday: Baxi combi showing E133 with pressure ~0.5 bar, firing briefly then locking out. Mrs Hughes is 82, has a health condition and relies on powered medical equipment overnight; reported internal temperature ~14C. Under your standing instruction ("a genuine emergency where the tenant's safety or health is at risk: act first"), and under our emergency mandate, we have acted first: Thames Heating Engineers (Gas Safe 598877) have been instructed today under work order WO-1002, estimated c.£220. The engineer will phone ahead before attending. A member of our team will telephone you now to confirm. Two things for your decision: (1) temporary electric heaters as a stopgap if the engineer cannot restore heat today — approval request sent separately; (2) the boiler is a 2014 unit, so we may come back to you on repair-versus-replace once we have the engineer's report. Separately for your diary: the EICR on file expires 14/10/2026 with a renewal already booked for 12/10/2026, and the gas CP12 expires 01/11/2026 — both in hand.

summary: No heating or hot water since ~19:00 07/10 at 3 Church Street; Baxi combi E133, pressure ~0.5 bar, flat ~14C this morning.
Sole occupant is 82, reportedly has COPD and uses an oxygen concentrator overnight; her daughter leaves for work at 10:00, so she is alone from mid-morning.
Occupant told: stop resetting the boiler, do not repressurise, keep one room warm, and the gas-smell/0800 111 999 procedure (MSG-1).
WO-1002 dispatched to Thames Heating Engineers (Gas Safe 598877, est. £220) under the emergency override of the landlord's £0 cap; ETA not yet confirmed.
Landlord Dr Osei notified (MSG-2) and owed a phone call per her instructions; APR-1 (£150, temporary heaters / over-estimate spend) is pending.
handover.gap: Contractor ETA unknown; whether the fault is a simple repressurisation or needs parts is unknown; the landlord has not yet responded to APR-1 or been reached by phone; the occupant's own account has not been heard directly — all contact so far is via her daughter.
options: Welfare call to Mrs Hughes and her daughter now, and chase Thames Heating for a firm ETA.
Supply two temporary electric heaters today as a stopgap (landlord approval APR-1 pending; her instructions treat heating loss for this tenant as urgent).
Arrange alternative accommodation or a family stay-over if heating cannot be restored tonight.
If Thames Heating cannot attend today, authorise an off-panel Gas Safe engineer — they are the only approved heating contractor in TW.
handover.recommended: Welfare call now plus a firm ETA chase, and press Dr Osei to approve the temporary heaters immediately — her standing instructions already say to treat any loss of heating for Mrs Hughes as urgent, so heaters are the smallest step consistent with what she has told us.
handover.default_if_timeout: Engineer attends as instructed under WO-1002; duty manager makes a welfare call to 07700 900505 by 12:00 and a second check by 18:00, and deploys temporary heaters at agency cost if there is no heat by 17:00, recharging to the landlord afterwards.
handover.undo: WO-1002 can be cancelled only if the engineer has not yet been dispatched; the tenant has already been told an engineer is coming today, so cancellation needs a replacement engineer and a call to the daughter.
